method: Pinned source functions with explicit dependency injection; no full-product execution

results.name: IDE Plan only filters built-in write tools
results.observation: Plan exposes an enabled external tool even with readonly=false.

results.name: IDE explicit tool/group exclusions
results.observation: Explicit disabled and group exclude remove tools before invocation.

results.name: Workspace boundary tightens file access
results.observation: Outside-workspace changes allow to ask, while disabled remains disabled.

results.name: Search replacement includes relaxed match strategies
results.observation: Exact, trimmed, case-insensitive and whitespace-ignored strategies are active; Jaro is disabled.

results.name: Ambiguous replacement is rejected unless replace_all
results.observation: Duplicate matches fail single replacement; replace_all changes both occurrences.

results.name: MultiEdit applies operations to successive string states
results.observation: Later edits see earlier results; string computation failure returns no new content (no disk atomicity claim).

results.name: CLI headless permissions retain earlier write ask rules
results.observation: First match wins: headless Edit=ask, Bash=allow, external fallback=allow.

results.name: CLI Plan permits Bash and unmatched MCP tools
results.observation: Plan is a tool policy preset, not an OS-level read-only environment.

results.name: CLI dynamic ask does not override static allow
results.observation: With an injected dynamic evaluator, only disabled overrides the configured allow.

results.name: CLI auto-compaction uses capped buffer arithmetic
CLI emergency pruning removes from the tail
results.observation: Tail user/assistant or adjacent assistant-tool pairs can be removed; this differs from IDE head pruning.

results.name: Compaction view preserves leading system message
results.observation: The LLM view starts from the compaction marker plus a retained leading system message.

results.name: MCP normalization is not collision-free
results.observation: Different server display names can normalize to the same prefix; use distinct configuration names.
